flawed_step: The step in a Tutte-condition proof that asserts every odd component of G-S sends at least 3 edges to S. That step needs the graph to be bridgeless; with a bridge, an odd component can send just 1 edge, so the count 3*odd(G-S) <= 3|S| fails.
counterexample: Block: K4 on {a,b,c,d} with edge ab deleted, plus a vertex e joined to a and b. Degrees: a,b,c,d have degree 3 and e has degree 2; the block has 5 vertices. Take three disjoint copies (a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i,e_i for i=1,2,3) and a centre vertex v joined to e_1,e_2,e_3. The graph is simple, connected and 3-regular on 16 vertices. There is no perfect matching: v is matched to exactly one e_i, so the other two blocks would each need a perfect matching within 5 vertices, which is impossible because 5 is odd. Equivalently, removing S={v} leaves 3 odd components, and 3 > |S| = 1, so Tutte's condition fails.
assessment_summary: False. Petersen's theorem needs the bridgeless hypothesis. The 16-vertex cubic graph made of three 5-vertex blocks (K4 minus an edge, with that edge subdivided) joined to a central vertex by bridges is connected and 3-regular but has no perfect matching.
